referees.quote: I therefore recommend that the authors revise the manuscript and address the points above before it can be considered for publication in Nature Communications.
I find the results—though well executed—somewhat disappointing in terms of their physical significance. The interpretation could also be further developed.
I am convinced by the validity of the results and the balanced conclusions... I generally support publication after the authors have addressed the below comments

note: The file starts at Version 0 at Nature Communications, with no transfer from another journal; only the Version 0 reports were used. No referee uses the scale terms, so all three levels are inferred. R1 says the issues 'prevent this referee from recommending publication' and asks for reorganization plus stronger justification of the topological-defect and amplitude/phase claims, which points to major revision. R2 is the least certain call. It gives no explicit verdict, questions the significance, calls the topological scenario 'naive', and says the paper is 'difficult to accept... unless the ref 4 has been published'. Its points are mostly addressable alternative explanations and clarifications, so major revision was chosen over reject, but a reject reading is defensible. R3's requests are small clarifications and figure fixes, so minor revision. All referees are individual reports; none co-signs another's report.
